ⓐ.summary: Heat generated during combustion is produced when caloric in gaseous oxygen is released and escapes into the air as oxygen combines with the substance.

c1.text: ⓐ In the process of combustion, the oxygen in gaseous oxygen combines with the burning substance to form a compound, but the caloric in gaseous oxygen does not combine with the substance and escapes into the air, thus generating heat.

c2.text: Heat is a massless substance called caloric, and the generation of heat is a process by which combined caloric is released.

c3.text: Gases contain far more caloric than solids or liquids.

c4.text: Gaseous oxygen is a compound of oxygen and caloric.

c5.text: Combustion of a substance is a process in which the substance combines with oxygen.

h1.text: When many solid substances combust, heat is generated and gas is produced at the same time.

h2.text: When a solid combusts to produce a gas, caloric from gaseous oxygen is absorbed into the gaseous product, so little or no caloric escapes into the air.

a.note: The tempting inference ra1 (that observing heat generation supports ⓐ) is undercut by ra2, because converting a solid to gas absorbs caloric rather than releasing it.

h3.text: Gunpowder contains solid oxygen compounds and can combust explosively and release massive heat even without gaseous oxygen.

h4.text: Heat generated during combustion is not caused by caloric escaping from gaseous oxygen.

b.note: Gunpowder combusts and releases heat without gaseous oxygen, providing an undefeated rebuttal against ⓐ.

h5.text: No matter how much heat generated during combustion is released into the air, the mass of air does not increase.

h6.text: Caloric is not released into the air during combustion.

c.note: The tempting rebuttal rc1 is undercut by caloric being massless (c2), so the air not gaining mass does not weaken ⓐ.
